body:
Synthetic World Generator. Creates internally consistent virtual worlds with terrain, weather, physics, ecosystems, buildings, and autonomous inhabitants.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 73 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Simulated Worlds and Reality-Scale Models". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: demonstrated. Procedural world generation ships in games (No Man's Sky: 18 quintillion planets); scientific consistency is the frontier.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Synthetic World Generator - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Creates internally consistent virtual worlds with terrain, weather, physics, ecosystems, buildings, and autonomous inhabitants.
body:
Known science foundations of Synthetic World Generator.

No Man's Sky generates vast explorable worlds. Minecraft's terrain generation is iconic. Unreal Engine 5 renders photorealistic environments. AI world models (Genie, Sora-class) generate interactive scenes. Internally consistent physics, ecosystems, and autonomous inhabitants at civilization scale remain research-grade.

Key quantity check (No Man's Sky planets in quintillions / hand-designed game worlds): computed ratio 0.18 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Synthetic World Generator - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Creates internally consistent virtual worlds with terrain, weather, physics, ecosystems, buildings, and autonomous inhabitants.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Synthetic World Generator.

Consistency breaks at boundaries between generators. Autonomous inhabitants need real AI, not scripts. Scientific fidelity costs more than entertainment needs.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 17.26 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is generated planets vs hand-designed at 17.26 orders of magnitude (generated planets larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
